title: Tomy learns what "proof of funds" means
caption: "Proof of funds" confuses so many students 😵 It's simply evidence you can pay for your studies and living costs: bank statements, sponsor letters, scholarship letters. Rules differ by country. Save this 📌 #proofoffunds #studentvisa #studyabroad

scenes.backdrop: cozy student bedroom at night with fairy lights and papers on the bed

beats.text: Quddus, the embassy says I need proof of funds. Is that like proof of life?
beats.say: Kuddus, the embassy says I need proof of funds. Is that like proof of life?
Close. It's proof that you can pay for your tuition and your living costs while you study.
So like... a picture of my piggy bank?
More like official documents. And each country sets its own amount and rules.

scenes.backdrop: modern café next to a bank with glass windows and plants

beats.say: Usually it's bank statements, a sponsor letter with their statements, or a scholarship letter that shows what's covered.
Some countries ask for money to stay in the account for a long time, right?
Yes. Some want it there for weeks or months, and some use special accounts like a blocked account. Always read the official visa page.
My uncle said he can lend me money for one day, just for the statement.
No! Sudden big deposits look suspicious, and fake documents can get you banned. Be honest and plan early.
Honest money, early planning. Got it!
